thread:
maya (support): Heads-up — customer SAM in prod reporting that our autorouter invoked `apply_credit` instead of `refund_payment` for a refund API call. They hit this from the public API, not internal UI.

sam (customer): FYI the user saw their balance updated as store credit. We sent payload with `amount": 24.00` and `currency": "USD"` — expected a refund to card.

maya (support): Repro steps from customer: 1) POST /v1/support/actions with tool hint null, 2) body: `{\n  "intent": "refund",\n  "amount": "24.00",\n  "currency": "USD",\n  "reason": "order_12345"\n}` 3) response OK but card not refunded.

elliot (eng): Hmm. Did they include `amount` as string vs numeric? Autorouter heuristics look at schema shapes and names. If `apply_credit` accepts `amount` string and `refund_payment` expects `amount_cents` int it could fuzzy-match.

maya (support): Customer said they never set `amount_cents`. Just top-level `amount` in dollars.

elliot (eng): Can you paste the server-side invocation log? runtime-bot should have trace id.

runtime-bot: trace=tr_8a3f. Router matched tool: `billing.apply_credit_v2` (confidence 0.62). Fallbacks: none. Payload forwarded: `{\n  "amount": "24.00",\n  "currency": "USD",\n  "reason": "order_12345"\n}`

julia (oncall): :eyes: confidence 0.62 is borderline. We recently lowered signature-strictness for autorouter to tolerate minor schema drift, maybe that made this worse.

elliot (eng): That hits exactly: `apply_credit_v2` has parameter `amount` (string, dollars) while `refund_payment` signature uses `amount_cents` (int) + `payment_method_id`. Fuzzy match prioritized parameter name overlap (amount) and shorter mismatch penalty.

maya (support): Customer needs immediate remediation — can we revert or force explicit tool mapping for their org?

elliot (eng): Short-term: we can add a per-customer routing override (pin to refund_payment) and a quick validation rule that rejects requests that lack `payment_method_id` when intent=refund. I'll open SRE ticket.

sam (customer): Appreciate the fast workaround. We do send payment_method in other flows but this one comes from webhook augmentation that strips it. Bad chain on our side too.

julia (oncall): Action items: 1) eng add routing override for sam-corp org id  (contact support to confirm) 2) prod alert for fuzzy-match confidence < 0.7 that causes a potential money-op mismatch 3) short doc for support on fields that must be present for refund flows.

elliot (eng): Working on PR: change autorouter scoring to penalize string->int type mismatches higher, and require exact `payment_method_id` presence for refund intent. Will target hotfix branch and roll to canary.

maya (support): I'll DM SAM to confirm contact info and schedule the override. Also escalating to billing eng channel to double-check ledger reconciliation for affected user.

runtime-bot: deploy started: canary autorouter-hotfix -> infra-canary-3 (deploy id dpl_992).

elliot (eng): After canary, we'll monitor traces for `apply_credit_v2` calls triggered by refund intent. If we see >0 matches in last 30m, rollback.

sam (customer): Confirmed override applied by maya — we see the refund call hit `refund_payment` now and card was charged back. Thanks.

maya (support): Closing loop: we gave the customer a rollback-safe override + asked eng for scoring change + created an internal KB. Adding note in ticket with trace tr_8a3f.

julia (oncall): Postmortem checklist: decide if autorouter default strictness needs global change, evaluate edge cases where currency units (dollars vs cents) are ambiguous, and add example payloads to public docs.

elliot (eng): I'll schedule follow-up for next week with ML/heuristics owners.

maya (support): Thanks team — marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
